approachQuestion.prompt:
Mirror Badge

A badge is a string s of lowercase English letters. Return true if deleting at most one character can make the remaining string read identically from left to right and right to left; otherwise return false. An empty string and a one-letter string satisfy the condition. The input cannot be modified.

Constraints: 0 <= n = s.length <= 200000. Indexed character access and comparison take constant time; every character is one byte.

Example 1: s = "abca" -> true (delete either b or c).
Example 2: s = "abcda" -> false.
Example 3: s = "deeee" -> true (delete d).
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Compare characters from both ends until the first mismatch at l,r. If none occurs, return true. Otherwise test both ranges [l+1,r] and [l,r-1] for exact symmetry using iterative index scans, returning true if either passes.
options.feedback: Any successful deletion must resolve the first mismatch. These two range checks cover both possibilities without allowing a second deletion.

options.text: Find the first mismatch in the same way, then copy s[l+1:r+1] and s[l:r] into new strings and test each for exact symmetry by indexed scans. Accept if either passes.
options.feedback: Both possible deletions are covered correctly. Copying the candidate substrings adds removable storage and copying work.

options.text: At the first mismatch discard the left character and check the remaining range for exact symmetry. Never try discarding the right character.
options.feedback: For "abcbab", deleting the final b yields "abcba", but dropping the first a leaves "bcbab", which fails.

options.text: At the first mismatch, discard the left character if the next left character equals the right character; otherwise discard the right character. Check only the chosen remainder.
options.feedback: For "abcbab", the next left b matches the right b, so this chooses the failing left deletion and misses the successful right deletion.

feedback.reason: At the first mismatch, exhaust both possible single deletions with bounded range checks rather than making an unjustified local choice.
details: Compare matching outer characters. At the first unequal pair, check the interior range obtained by skipping the left character and the range obtained by skipping the right character. Each check allows no further deletions. Accept if either range is symmetric.

At the first mismatch, at least one of those two characters must be deleted. Test those two remaining ranges without permitting another deletion. Deleting an unrelated interior character cannot repair the mismatched outer pair.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair, with n equal to the original input length. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed reads, writes, comparisons, and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include every temporary buffer, copy, and call frame. The fixed method is iterative, makes no input copy, uses no hashing, and performs no amortized data-structure operations. Exclude the supplied input and returned scalar; include all other storage. No recursion, slices, or allocated work arrays are used.
constraints: Choose the tightest pair for this fixed method, regardless of the approach you selected in question 1.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: At most three bounded scans use indices into the original string.
details: The initial scan and at most two range scans each visit at most n positions. All-same-letter strings force a linear initial scan. The checks use indices into the original string, with no slices or recursion.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed reads, writes, comparisons, and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include every temporary buffer, copy, and call frame. The fixed method is iterative, makes no input copy, uses no hashing, and performs no amortized data-structure operations. Exclude the supplied input and returned scalar; include all other storage. No recursion, slices, or allocated work arrays are used.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This adds a size-dependent temporary copy or buffer absent from the fixed method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The method does not restart a full scan for each element; its bounded number of forward or inward scans is linear.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: No sorting or repeated binary searches occur in the fixed method.
